assessment: Major revision required: the printed target-independent local factors make the main asymptotic formula false, and the general symmetric near-extremizer subgroup lemma is false; eight local findings have bounded repairs.
outcome: Two confirmed Major and eight confirmed Minor findings. Exact-source initial scientific review complete; independent scientific acceptance pending.

problems.title: The main local density counts zero instead of the target N
problems.location: Theorem 1.1 and (1.3), p.2; beta_infinity p.3; orthogonality p.12
problems.hypotheses_checked: Q=2 sum_{i=1}^4 (x_i-y_i)(i x_i+(i+1)y_i), N=1. a=2diag(1,2,3,4), b=2I, c=-2diag(2,3,4,5); det(ab) nonzero and Delta=diag(-9,-25,-49,-81) has distinct eigenvalues avoiding -1 and0.
problems.decisive_evidence: Every integer value is even, so the count is0. The printed zero-level factors are positive: beta_2=4; all odd unit zeros are nonsingular and exist; binary Gauss sums give beta_p=1+O(p^-3), so the infinite product is positive. An interior regular zero gives beta_infinity uniformly positive for large X. Thus asserted main term >=c X^6 contradicts zero with o(X^6) error. Exact18-case residue calculations corroborate the proof.
problems.impact: The exact printed main theorem is false under its full hypotheses.
problems.repair: Change congruence Q=0 to Q=N in (1.3); corrected beta_2(1)=0 for this witness.
problems.repair_limit: The intended theorem with corrected factors is not refuted; no transfer to the journal version.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Theorem1.1/(1.3) p.2, real density p.3 and target-dependent orthogonality p.12. The local congruence is literally zero, despite the target N notation.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: Q=2 sum_i(x_i-y_i)(i x_i+(i+1)y_i), N=1 has integer coefficients, a=2diag(1,2,3,4), b=2I, c=-2diag(2,3,4,5), det(ab) nonzero and Delta=diag(-9,-25,-49,-81), all distinct and outside{-1,0}. No primitivity requirement excludes it.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The count is identically zero by parity. For odd p at least one binary block is nonsingular, so every unit zero has nonzero gradient; all-ones supplies a zero. Hensel lifts give positive stabilized local factors. For p>7 each full split binary Gauss sum is p for nonzero frequency, with unit restriction bounded by p+2sqrt(p)+1, hence beta_p=1+O(p^-3) and a positive convergent Euler product. At2, nonsingularity of Q/2 on unit residues gives unit zero count 2^(7n-6) for n>=2, so beta2=4. The interior zero x=y=(1/2,...,1/2) is regular; its real-density patch stays positive as N/X^2 tends to0. Thus the printed main term is at least cX^6, incompatible with the zero count and o(X^6) error.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Replacing Q=0 by Q=N makes the 2-adic factor zero for N=1. This witness then supplies no contradiction.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Exact printed principal asymptotic is false under all stated hypotheses, Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Correct the target congruence consistently. No falsity of the intended theorem or the 2025 journal version is inferred.

problems.title: Symmetric Young near-extremizers may lie on a nonidentity coset
problems.location: Lemma C.2 p.52; (C.4) and Corollary C.3 p.53; Section9 Step2 p.34
problems.hypotheses_checked: On C2={e,s}, s^2=e and mu=delta_s is a symmetric probability with ||mu*mu||_2=||mu||_2=1 for every epsilon. It also embeds at -I in Sp8(Fp), odd p.
problems.decisive_evidence: Squared distances to uniform subgroup measures in C2 are2 and1/2, so no O(epsilon^c) closeness as epsilon tends to0. Symmetry does not remove coset shifts. The squared norm hypothesis printed in C.2 is vacuous for every symmetric probability since (mu*mu)(e)=||mu||_2^2. C3 measure(1/2,1/4,1/4) independently confirms this normalization issue. Fournier Theorem3 gives equality up to translations.
problems.impact: False general auxiliary lemma supplies (9.6)-(9.8), Proposition8.4 and amplification Proposition6.2; this is a core dependency.
problems.repair: Prove a correctly normalized positive-definite/even-convolution version sufficient for the actual measure, or prove coset elimination from that additional structure.
problems.repair_limit: Actual Section9 measures are positive semidefinite; delta_s is not. No counterexample to Proposition8.4 for those measures or to the corrected main theorem is claimed.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Counting norm and C.2 p.52, C.4 and C.3 p.53, invocation (9.6)-(9.8) p.34. Symmetrized convolution is defined pp.26-27.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: In C2, mu=delta_s with s^2=e is a symmetric probability. Both convolution and original norms equal1; the example also embeds at -I in Sp8 over every odd prime.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Squared distances to the only subgroup uniforms are2 and1/2, precluding any uniform O(epsilon^c) conclusion. Symmetry allows a nonidentity coset. Independently, C.2's printed squared-norm hypothesis is automatic because (mu*mu)(e)=||mu||^2<=||mu*mu||. For C3 mu=(1/2,1/4,1/4), exact norms squared3/8 and43/128 and distance squared1/24 to uniform confirm the normalization defect even with nonnegative Fourier spectrum. Fournier's actual equality argument explicitly translates to a subgroup and recovers a coset.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Actual nu=(mu_opposite*mu)^(2^(t-1)) has a positive-semidefinite convolution operator; delta_s has a negative eigenvalue and is not such a nu. A correctly normalized special lemma may succeed.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: The false general statement is the stated justification for (9.6)-(9.8), then Proposition8.4, Proposition8.2 and amplification6.2. This demonstrated core derivation error is Major without a counterexample to the special proposition.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Prove an adequate correctly normalized positive-semidefinite near-extremizer result, or justified coset elimination from the actual structure. Success of that repair is not assumed.

problems.title: Wrong integral dimension and Fourier localization normalization
problems.hypotheses_checked: Pairs are eight-dimensional; X=2, bounded constant weights, eta=0 and integral phase; smooth cutoff on R8 for the repaired estimate.
problems.decisive_evidence: Discrete [X]^4 pairs have zero Lebesgue measure whereas I(0)=X^8. Printed w:R2 and cube[0,1]^12 are incompatible with eight variables. Equation(6.11) expectation gives1 instead of256. Two derivatives per R4 block do not yield integrable decay. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz with (1+|xi|^2/t^2)^3 and Plancherel derivatives through6 rigorously gives Fourier L1 O(t^4).
problems.impact: Displayed definitions and proof estimates need correction.
problems.repair: Use R8 measure and continuous[0,X]^4, w onR8 equal1 on[0,1]^8, unnormalized sum, and report estimate(R9).
problems.repair_limit: The repaired localization preserves M^5 and does not refute Proposition3.4.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: The p.13 f_epsilon uses R4 measure and discrete [X]^4 for eight real variables. Actual p.19 image confirms R2 and cube[0,1]^12; (6.11) is an expectation although S is a sum.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For X=2, eta=0 and an integral phase with constant weights, the original S has256 terms. Fourier localization requires u,v in R4, hence eight dimensions.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: A literal discrete set has zero Lebesgue measure, whereas I(0)=X^8. The displayed expectation equals1 instead of256. Decay of order2 in each R4 block is not integrable. For the repair let t=1+|lambda|: Cauchy-Schwarz with weight (1+|xi|^2/t^2)^3 gives a first factor O(t^4); Plancherel and derivatives through order6 of w exp(2pi i lambda Q) give a bounded second factor. Thus Fourier L1=O(t^4) is justified in R8.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The exponent4 in the desired Fourier bound is achievable, so the downstream M^5 conclusion is not refuted. The apparent cube exponent2 from extraction was disproved by actual image inspection.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Dimension/normalization and written proof errors with a complete local analytic repair, Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Use R8, continuous[0,X]^4 pairs, cutoff on[0,1]^8, an unnormalized sum and the weighted L2 argument.

problems.hypotheses_checked: The exact sequences in the report satisfy all inequalities used in the abstract deduction: alpha positive <=alpha_star, beta nondecreasing in[0,36], alpha nonincreasing on constant-beta runs.
problems.decisive_evidence: alpha_star(1)=1, alpha_star(j>=2)=10; explicit10-step descending runs reset at36 jumps. Printed T37=352; first simultaneous adjacent equality at361. All362 rows independently verified.
problems.impact: The printed quantitative deduction from Lemma9.2 inequalities is invalid.
problems.repair: Use S1=alpha_star(1), S_{i+1}=S_i+1+alpha_star(S_i+1), and correct the earlier endpoint+1.
problems.repair_limit: This is an abstract-sequence counterexample, not an asserted measure sequence. Qualitative O(1) stabilization survives; example repaired bound397.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: Lemma9.2 supplies positivity, bounded beta and monotonicity pp.31-32; Proposition9.3 pp.33-34 uses T_(i+1)=T_i+alpha_star(T_i) and overlooks post-jump resets.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: alpha_star(1)=1 and alpha_star(j>=2)=10 is nondecreasing. Set(alpha1,beta1)=(1,0); for2<=j<=361 set alpha=10-((j-2) mod10), beta=min(36,1+floor((j-2)/10)); thereafter(1,36). All362 checked rows obey the exact inequalities invoked.

problems.title: Every splitting type need not occur for a fixed generic form
problems.hypotheses_checked: P1 generic form has characteristic polynomial(T+9)(T+25)(T+49)(T+81).
problems.decisive_evidence: For every p>7 all four roots are distinct in Fp, hence Fp[Delta]=Fp^4; no other degree partition occurs.
problems.impact: The stated occurrence claim exceeds genericity assumptions.
problems.repair: Delete universal occurrence wording or add an appropriate Galois-group assumption.
problems.repair_limit: The proof treats every possible type and does not require all to occur.

independent_acceptance.source_fidelity: After classifying the five possible quartic factorization types, p.43 says all can be expected as p varies for the fixed discriminant.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses_checked: For the fully generic P1 form the characteristic polynomial is(T+9)(T+25)(T+49)(T+81); all pairwise differences have prime factors at most7.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Every p>7 has four distinct rational roots, so Fp[Delta] is always Fp^4. Genericity alone cannot force another splitting type.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: All five types are legitimate possibilities across different forms; the proof's case analysis needs only that exhaustive list, not occurrence for each form.
independent_acceptance.dependency_and_severity: Unsupported universal occurrence assertion outside the proof dependency, Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_scope: Remove the occurrence sentence or impose an appropriate Galois-group condition; no effect on the case classification.

limitations: The main formula is refuted exactly as printed with Q=0 local congruences. The intended theorem with Q=N factors is not refuted.
The C2 counterexample refutes the general CorollaryC.3, not Proposition8.4 for the actual positive-semidefinite convolution measures. An adequate replacement lemma still requires proof.
P8 disproves the abstract inference from the inequalities used, not an asserted sequence produced by the actual measures.

The Lang-Weil coefficient and p>=5 formulation are clarifications without a counterexample to the paper's actual collision varieties or small-prime group claim; neither is counted as a confirmed issue.
